:::{#exm-binary-variable}
#### A binary variable is an indicator

In a study of $n$ people,
let $s_i = 1$ if person $i$ smokes and $s_i = 0$ otherwise,
for $i \in \cb{1, \ldots, n}$.
Then $s_i$ is a binary variable (@def-binary-variable).
It is also the predicate indicator (@def-indicator-function)
of the proposition "person $i$ smokes":
$s_i = \indicp{\text{person } i \text{ smokes}}$.

In the same way,
every indicator is a binary variable,
and every binary variable $X$ is the indicator of its own value being $1$:
$X = \indicp{X = 1}$,
since both sides are $1$ when $X = 1$ and $0$ when $X = 0$.

:::
